text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - The London market turned in another disappointing performance after falling back to eight-week lows as interest rate worries and dollar weakness took a toll on share prices. An initial 17-point climb on the back of the Dow's election-inspired surge overnight swiftly evaporated as FTSE futures and gilts led the market lower. The FTSE 100 closed 35.3 points lower at 3,900.4.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX index ended floor dealings lower, dragged down by a sharp fall in the shares of German electronic firm Siemens, which had already tumbled in Wednesday's post-bourse electronic trade. The DAX index closed floor trade down 15.97 points, or 0.59 percent, at 2,713.22, off the day's low of 2,703.96. In post-bourse trade the index was down 11.03 at 2724.25.

PARIS - French shares closed just below Wednesday's closing high, maintaining a level not seen since early 1994 as Wall Street bounced back from opening losses on profit-taking. The Paris market had been in the red all day and the blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 1.56 points or 0.07 percent at 2,211.81.

ZURICH - Swiss shares were pressured by profit taking and closed lower despite a late recovery due to a friendly opening on Wall Street. The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended down 3.9 points, or 0.1 percent, to 3,811.5 points. The broad SPI was down 3.99 points, or 0.16 percent, to 2,438.87.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks gave up earlier gains to close sharply lower, after buying momentum carried over from the previous day was watered down by the yen's rises against the dollar and sporadic sales by foreign investors. The key 225-share Nikkei average slipped 220.41 points, or 1.05 percent, to finish at 20,771.11.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks and index futures zigzagged throughout the day to close lower as euphoria over the U.S. election was dampened by fears of profit-taking on Wall Street. The Hang Seng Index closed down 40.21 points at 12,735.26 after setting a new intraday high of 12,898.30 in early morning trading.

SYDNEY - A lacklustre performance by Australian shares despite a 96-point rise by the Dow Jones industrial average and a local interest rate cut on Wednesday underscored the mediocre outlook for Australian corporate earnings and the stock market itself. The All Ordinaries index closed 13.9 points lower at 2,346.7 as the market ignored the Dow's post-election jump and a 0.5 percent cut in Austrlian official interest rates on Wednesday.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended a grim Thursday down for the fourth consecutive session, hit by a wave of negative sentiment that has sent prices tumbling. The market is worried over confusing signals from government and the Reserve Bank on scrapping exchange controls and rising fears of an interest rate hike. The all-share index climbed a little from its day lows, but still ended at 6,802.9, down 71.0 points, as industrials slid to 8,014.4, down 77.1 points. Gold shares, which were resilient earlier in the week, suffered a second bad day running. The golds index fell 9.0 points to 1,693.0 over fears about a jittery bullion price.
